text:
maria: Observed spikes in 502s when clients reconnect to /v1/stream after brief network blips. Happens ~10-30s after idle. Any ideas?

ben: yup saw it in prod traces. Mostly clients behind CloudLB. Client reconnect -> new TCP -> routed to different backend -> backend rejects because old stream still marked reserved for a short lease.

chen: digging into logs: we set STREAM_LOCK in redis with a 25s lease during resume window. New connection checks Last-Event-ID but our resume logic aborts if lease is still held by previous session or if lease just expired -> race.

srebot: deploy-success: canary rolled to 2/5 at 2025-10-03T14:12:00Z

maria: thinking out loud: issue an ephemeral resume token in response headers (X-Resume-Token) that maps to an offset and is valid for 90s. Any backend could accept the token, look up offset and replay. Less reliance on sticky routing. Low-risk?

ben: feasible but needs routing/proxy changes. Today we rely on connection-id -> backend sticky. If a new connection carries a resume token, we either need a coordinator proxy that routes it to the original backend, or make event storage readable by any backend.

evan: alternative: keep current design, force clients to exponential-backoff and treat resume window as best-effort. Server returns 409 + Retry-After when resume fails and clients open a fresh stream. Simpler but worse UX.

maria: sample client pseudocode to opt-in resume:
```\nasync function connect() {\n  let retry = 0;\n  while (true) {\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch('/v1/stream', {\n        headers: {\n          'Last-Event-ID': lastId || '',\n          'X-Resume-Token': token || '',\n          'X-Resume-Opt-In': 'true'\n        }\n      });\n      // stream handling here\n    } catch (e) {\n      await sleep(expBackoff(retry++));\n    }\n  }\n}\n```

chen: telemetry we need: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_conflict(409), resume_latency, resume_route_miss. Add per-model and per-tenant filter to console so SRE/product can triage quickly.

ben: server implementation notes:
- issue token on initial open, store token->(offset, model, tenant) in redis with TTL=90s
- accept resume token on connect: if found -> mark session resumed and stream from stored offset
- if not found -> return 409 + Retry-After
- ensure resumed streams don't double-charge quota for already delivered tokens (idempotency)

maria: rollout plan idea:
- canary token issuance on canary fleet, collect resume_success and latency metrics
- enable token validation path in proxy (route to coordinator when token provided)
- behind feature flag enable X-Resume-Opt-In default off, flip on after metrics look good

evan: test plan: add flaky network simulation to integration harness, add LB connection kill at t=15s to reproduce race. E2E smoke where client disconnects and reconnects to different backend.

ben: question: are we better off moving to WebSockets? Pros: fewer HTTP proxy quirks, easier binary framing. Cons: infra work, some cloud LBs still kill idle WS similarly, and scale/ALB limits to consider.

maria: I prefer incremental: implement resume tokens for SSE first (smaller blast radius), evaluate websocket migration later if problems persist.

chen: created INF-2348 with design doc & sequence diagrams: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2348. I'll add metrics + patch for redis token store.

srebot: incident note: 2025-10-03 14:30 UTC - 1h - SSE resume race causing ~0.7% 502 uptick for customers with heavy streaming usage.

maria: thanks — I'll open the design PR and a console dashboard mock in #eng-platform. Assigning infra changes to @chen. Please drop short comments on the doc if you see issues. :thumbsup:
